note: Ground truth is derived from crAPI's OWN published challenge docs and locked (hash-sealed) BEFORE any ONYX run. It declares only the authorization challenges in ONYX's domain and honestly cedes the rest. Each known_vuln is a true positive (crAPI is intentionally vulnerable); each known_clean is a legitimate access that must NOT be flagged.

known_vulns.description: A user can read another user's vehicle GPS location by supplying a vehicle UUID they do not own.
Mechanic report IDs are sequential and unauthenticated; a user can read other users' reports by changing report_id.
The video resource exposes an internal property that should not be visible to the user (excessive data exposure).
A non-admin user can reach an admin-only endpoint to delete videos (function-level authorization).
The order object accepts a client-supplied `status` field; changing 'delivered' to 'returned' yields an unwarranted refund (mass assignment).

known_clean.description: A user reading the location of THEIR OWN vehicle — a legitimate 200 a status/length heuristic would also flag.
A user reading their OWN mechanic report.
A user reading their OWN order details (no status mutation).
A user reading their OWN dashboard/profile — rich shape by design, not a leak.

ceded.reason: brute force, not a Δstate authorization differential
